extractor.note: Partial pass over Supplement II, § 2 and Text Nr. 5, where the reduction and the epoché carry argumentative weight.

coverage_note: Covers Supplement II (pre-givenness and affectivity), § 2 (the world pre-given as cultural world pointing back to nature) and Text Nr. 5 (the pure experiential world). The remaining texts of the volume carry hits and are not covered.

units.claim: Only phenomenology, under the title of the phenomenological reduction, has gone beyond the ordinary sporadic bringing-to-prominence of the subjective.
units.quote: But only phenomenology, in its method under the title "phenomenological reduction," has gone beyond the ordinary sporadic bringing-to-prominence of the subjective.

units.claim: Carrying out the phenomenological attitude already presupposes having the world of transcendental questions as horizon, so the epoché rests on a motivational structure of its own.
units.quote: carrying out the phenomenological attitude already presupposes that we have the "world" of transcendental questions as horizon

units.claim: Through the reduction the previously anonymous subjectivity is opened as a total field of investigation and the object-world is re-situated as what appears within subjective life.
units.quote: Through the phenomenological reduction, the previously anonymous subjectivity is opened up as a total field of investigation, and the object-world is re-situated as that which appears within subjective life.

units.claim: The constitution of intersubjectivity begins from a reduction to the primordial sphere of what is immediately-originally given to me alone.
units.quote: (1) reduction to the primordial sphere of what is immediately-originally given to me alone

units.claim: A reduction to mere, pure nature can be carried out within the experiential world, so that a structure 'nature' runs unitarily through it.
units.quote: One can carry out a reduction to mere, pure nature. Thus a structure "nature" runs unitarily through the experiential world.

units.claim: It is asked what the method of subjecting the general thesis of the world to an epoché means, given that the world with all subjects is found as a constituted unity.
units.quote: What does the method mean — to subject the "general thesis" of the world to an epoché?
